summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (60/112)

data.turoyo: Aḥ ḥawronaṯṯe hawən kar, af farxaṯṯe rawən, hawən rabe, maftalle foṯayye laf i barriye.
data.translation: Inzwischen machten sich die Gefährten reisefertig; ihre Jungen waren groß geworden, sie machten sich auf nach der Steppe.

rationale: Thin existing I Preterit Intransitive cell; a full chicks-growing-up context replaces neither the inherited isolated rawən form nor its grammar reference.

summary: I rawən at 60/112 is plural growth with the young as affected subject, confirmed by hawən rabe. It belongs to the inherited grow homonym, not rwy 2 intoxication.

The read-only lookup confirms rby I rabi/robe for growth and rby II mrabele/mrabe for raising/nourishing. This supports comparison of rby and rwy 1 as variant families but does not by itself assign moráwlalan to either.

The exact upbringing token moráwlalan is already preserved in the tly note tlele ŭ maḥatle, with Nisane first-interview attribution. It is new evidence for deciding lexical ownership, not discovery of an otherwise unattested word.
The grandmother is agent and -lan indexes the children. This is causative upbringing in meaning; it cannot safely determine the stem from translation when the root and internal form remain disputed.
No new III base forms, sense or box are published. The proposal is retained as a rejected-for-publication sense decision and a concrete question, rather than asserted as an established paradigm.
Which entry and stem own moráwlalan: rwy 1 III, a variant of rby II, or another causative? Confirm the transcription and morpheme boundaries with a speaker; only one unusual token is available.
Should rwy 1 and rby receive explicit reciprocal cross-references for the growth/upbringing family, while retaining the separate rwy 2 intoxication homonym? No other entry is changed in this run.
